data.title: Python analysis layer (analysis/) + core feature extractors
data.body:
## Goal
Stand up the `analysis/` Python package (numpy / scipy / soundfile / librosa) that turns a render WAV into a metrics JSON — the home of every feature extractor regimes B and C consume (strategy §2.2). Kept in a different language from the DSP on purpose, so a bug isn't mirrored in both the synth and its own test.

## Scope
- Package scaffold under `analysis/` with deps pinned; `analyze(wav_path, feature_set) -> metrics` entry point + small CLI.
- Core extractors: peak / RMS / DC offset; spectral centroid; decay / energy envelope (Hilbert); fundamental + partial-peak track; alias-floor estimate.
- Emit a stable, documented metrics JSON schema.

## Testing
- Unit tests on synthetic signals with known answers: pure sine → centroid & pitch; exponentially-decaying sine → decay time / envelope slope; DC and Nyquist edge cases.
- Smoke test on a placeholder-bleep WAV produced by `render` (880 Hz decaying sine): centroid ≈ 880 Hz, measured decay ≈ `BASE_TAU`, DC ≈ 0.

## Done when
Extractors pass the synthetic-truth tests and produce sane metrics on a bleep render; the metrics JSON schema is documented.

data.title: Regime-A invariant suite + no-alloc / no-panic gates (native cargo test)
data.body:
## Goal
The engine-agnostic correctness gates of strategy §4, run in `cargo test` (cheap) and behind `--full` (heavy). These are correctness, not taste, and are never blessed away. Validated now against the placeholder bleep; voice-specific guards (BD no-sweep, choke, metallic phase) ship with their voices.

## Scope (engine-wide invariants)
- Determinism bit-exact (compare via `f32::to_bits`; NaN must never appear).
- Buffer-size independence bit-exact across {64,128,256,512}.
- Sample-rate feature-correctness across {44.1,48,88.2,96 kHz} (features land; cross-rate output is not byte-compared).
- DC-free outputs; denormal-free tails that flush to exact zero.
- No allocation in `process()` — run the render scope under an allocation-flagging allocator (setup/teardown may allocate).
- No panics in `process()`.
- Parameter monotonicity (LEVEL monotonic gain; variance_depth=0 fully sterile/repeatable).
- Negative guard: no `load_sample` / PCM-asset path anywhere.

## Testing
Some of these already live in `dsp_core` tests (determinism, block-size, drive, isolation) — fold them in and complete the set. Heavy ones gated behind a `--full` feature/flag. All pass against the current bleep engine.

## Done when
The full engine-wide regime-A set is green in `cargo test` and under `--full`, on the bleep.

data.title: WASM↔native parity gate
data.body:
## Goal
Prove the two builds of `dsp_core` agree (strategy §5) — the assumption the entire "test native, ship wasm" approach rests on. Target bit-identical.

## Scope
- Render the same `RenderRequest` natively and on wasm32; diff the buffers. Pick the cheapest of: a `wasm32` core test target under wasmtime/wasmer, or `wasm-pack test --node` / `wasm-bindgen-test` on the streaming `Engine`. Do both (core + streaming) if feasible.
- Define a tight parity tolerance; treat any exceedance as a bug (usual culprit: a non-`mathx` transcendental, or an FP-reorder/fast-math flag leaking into one build).
- Streaming-vs-offline equivalence: events pushed one-at-a-time vs. the whole list up front must agree to the tolerance.

## Testing
Parity diff on bleep renders across the CI axes is bit-identical (or within the defined tolerance).

## Done when
The parity gate runs in CI and is green on the bleep; how to run the wasm side is documented.

data.title: dsp-harness MCP server (the calibration agent's hands)
data.body:
## Goal
The `harness/` `dsp-harness` MCP server wrapping `render` + `analysis`, exposing the strategy §2.3 tool surface so the calibration agent drives a tight loop instead of edit-and-pray.

## Scope (tool surface, §2.3)
- `render_voice(voice, sample_rate, block_size, seed, variance_depth, accent, events) -> wav_id` and `render_mix(request) -> wav_id`.
- `analyze(wav_id, feature_set) -> metrics_json` (wraps `analysis/`).
- `run_invariants(scope) -> report` (wraps the regime-A suite).
- `parity_check(request) -> max_divergence` (wraps the parity gate).
- `compare_to_targets(metrics, voice) -> deltas` (regime B) and `compare_to_reference(wav_id, voice) -> shape_distance` (regime C) — present with the metric plumbing; per-voice targets/clips fill in as voices land.
- `propose_param_edit` / `apply_param_edit` — the write side, scoped to calibratable constants only (never shipped control semantics).
- Calibration defaults sterile: variance_depth=0, fixed seed, fixed event placement.

## Testing
End-to-end against the bleep: `render_voice(bleep) → analyze → metrics`; `run_invariants` green; `parity_check` ≈ 0; `compare_*` return structured deltas against a trivial target set.

## Done when
The MCP server starts, every tool is callable, and the bleep round-trip (render → analyze → invariants → parity) works.

data.title: Goldens + --bless workflow
data.body:
## Goal
A golden is a frozen render plus its metric vector, guarding regimes B/C and the full mix against accidental drift; it is regenerated only by an explicit, reviewed `--bless` that emits a before/after diff (strategy §9). Regime-A invariants are never blessed away.

## Scope
- A golden store (render + metric vector) and a comparator that flags drift.
- `bless_golden(voice, reason) -> diff_report` as the only writer of a golden; it always emits the before/after diff for the one human glance.

## Testing
Create a bleep golden; re-render unchanged → no drift; perturb a constant → drift flagged; `bless` produces a readable before/after diff and refreshes the golden.

## Done when
Golden compare + bless round-trip works on the bleep and emits a diff report.

data.title: Bridged-T (Twin-T) resonator block
data.body:
## Goal
The core tonal building block (spec §3.1): a high-Q biquad bandpass that, pinged by a short pulse, rings as a naturally decaying sine whose decay rate is set by Q (`Q = sqrt(R1/R2) / (sqrt(C1/C2) + sqrt(C2/C1))`). Backbone of every tonal voice; the BD needs two of them.

## Scope
- Tier-A high-Q biquad bandpass, impulse/pulse excited, at host rate.
- Excited on trigger so the ring is phase-locked to the hit (the tonal-voice analog of "phase reset").
- Stable at high Q (no blow-up / NaN / Inf); denormal-clamped; tail flushes to exact zero.

## Testing (cargo test, native; strategy §3.1)
- Centre frequency and −3 dB bandwidth as designed.
- Decay-time tracks Q.
- High-Q stability: no NaN/Inf.
- Reset matches a fresh instance; block-size invariance bit-exact.

## Done when
The resonator hits its centre-freq / bandwidth / Q-decay targets and is numerically clean.

data.title: Trigger / excitation generator block
data.body:
## Goal
Shape the raw step trigger into the ~1 ms band-limited pulse that pings the resonators (spec §3.2, §2.3). Amplitude scales with accent; deterministic hit-to-hit (variance is added explicitly in §10, never as trigger sloppiness).

## Scope
- ~1 ms band-limited excitation pulse; accent scales amplitude (and therefore ring length).
- BLEP/BLAMP-style edge handling on the ping so the attack edge doesn't alias (spec §2.2 / §8).
- Fully deterministic given (seed, sample index).

## Testing (cargo test)
- Pulse width ≈ 1 ms across sample rates; amplitude scales monotonically with accent.
- Deterministic hit-to-hit; band-limited (alias floor under the bar).

## Done when
The generator emits a deterministic ~1 ms accent-scaled pulse with a clean edge.

data.title: RC exponential envelope + VCA with accent grit
data.body:
## Goal
Two small shared blocks the BD output stage needs: the decay-only RC (anti-log / exponential) amplitude envelope (spec §3.3) and the VCA = gain × mild saturation whose drive scales with accent (spec §3.9), so accented hits are grittier as well as louder.

## Scope
- RC envelope: exponential taper (never a linear ramp); time-constants clamped against denormals; tail flushes to exact zero.
- VCA: gain × a mild saturating nonlinearity; drive scales with excitation/accent level.

## Testing (cargo test)
- Envelope: exponential shape (≈ 1/e at the time-constant), not a linear ramp, exact-zero tail.
- VCA: near-linear at low level; added harmonic content rises with drive/accent; an accented hit is measurably grittier (more HF), not merely louder.

## Done when
Both blocks pass their shape/behaviour tests and are denormal-clean.

data.title: Bass-drum two-resonator voice assembly
data.body:
## Goal
Assemble the BD (spec §4.1): two Twin-T resonators — OSC1 ≈ 60 Hz Q≈7 (body/sustain), OSC2 ≈ 130 Hz Q≈3, lower amplitude and shorter (the click/attack) — pinged by ONE shared excitation edge so they start in phase and beat as they diverge. The signature solid, slightly clicky front edge is that brief in-phase moment, NOT a pitch sweep. Wire into `Engine`, replacing the BD bleep, behind the existing trigger / level / accent interface.

## Scope
- Instance two resonator blocks + one excitation + a gentle output VCA envelope; sum with OSC2 at lower level.
- Accent scales the excitation → longer + louder ring on both resonators (spec §2.3), not a pure output-gain change.
- No 808-style downward pitch sweep.

## Testing (cargo test; strategy §3.1 assembly + §4 regime-A BD guards)
- In-phase positive front edge; subsequent beating present.
- OSC2 lower amplitude and shorter than OSC1.
- **No downward pitch sweep**: pitch-track the sum — partials are stationary (the single most important "don't accidentally build an 808" guard).
- Determinism bit-exact; DC-free; tail to zero. The other six voices still bleep, unaffected.

## Done when
The BD plays a real two-resonator kick through the engine and passes the BD regime-A guards; other voices untouched.

data.title: Bass-drum regime-B numeric calibration
data.body:
## Goal
Close the regime-B loop (strategy §6, §11) on the BD: drive `render_voice → analyze → compare_to_targets → apply_param_edit` at variance_depth=0 / fixed seed until the spec numbers land within tolerance.

## Targets (spec §4.1)
- Dual-partial pitch ≈ 60 Hz & 130 Hz; Qs ≈ 7 & 3; OSC2 at lower relative level.
- In-phase attack-edge polarity; beat rate; pitch-track flatness (no sweep).

## Scope
- Gate on regime A first (`run_invariants`) — never tune fidelity on top of a broken invariant.
- Move only the mapped calibratable constants (the two resonator freqs/Qs, relative level, excitation). Flag any structural / Tier-B problem rather than chasing it with constants.
- Freeze numeric goldens for these targets.

## Testing
`compare_to_targets` deltas within tolerance for every BD target; numeric goldens captured; regime A still green.

## Done when
All BD §6 numeric targets are within tolerance and captured as goldens.

data.title: Bass-drum regime-C reference-clip calibration + golden
data.body:
## Goal
Anchor the BD default operating point to `references/bd.wav` on shape only (strategy §7, §11; spec §11) — never null tests, never loudness — then propose the human bless gate.

## Scope
- `compare_to_reference` on shape: two-resonator fit (60/130 Hz, Qs, relative level), confirm the in-phase attack edge + beating, no sweep. Aggregate a multi-resolution log-STFT shape distance, always reported alongside the decomposed per-feature deltas.
- Respect what regime C cannot fit: leave absolute level, accent, and variance depth as best-guess — do not let the loop "succeed" by drifting them.
- `parity_check` the result; then `bless_golden(bd, reason)` with a before/after diff for the one human glance.

## Testing
Shape distance + decomposed deltas within tolerance vs `bd.wav`; overlay plots (spectrogram, decay envelope, pitch track); parity max-divergence ≈ 0; bless diff produced for review.

## Done when
The BD matches `bd.wav` on shape, parity holds, and a blessed BD golden + diff await human sign-off.
